evidence.note: Upfront discovery then explicit dependency-DAG mapping via grep of `use rusternetes_common/storage/api_server` across crates — establishes dependency-aware ordering before coding.

Strict leaf-first compile milestones: common --no-run, then storage, then api-server, with re-verification of common+storage together (108) before advancing — deferring dependents until foundations verified.

Workspace-build milestone (303) followed by per-crate provided-test green in dependency order (306-308), then kubelet/scheduler, then workspace compile (413/429) and workspace test (433) — milestones tied to concrete build/test checks.

Decomposed the hardest crate (controller-manager) into per-test-binary checkpoints, running and greening each test file individually (replicaset, deployment, statefulset, pdb, ttl, endpoints, dynamic_provisioner, garbage_collector...), each with its own exit test — internal ordering within a large crate.

Explicit plan-tool updates appear only late/sparsely, indicating sequencing was emergent from build order rather than a living granular milestone hierarchy maintained from the start — short of the level-10 anchor.

reasoning: The agent demonstrated an explicit dependency-aware, leaf-to-root sequence (common→storage→api-server→controller-manager→kubelet→scheduler→kubectl) with milestones tied to concrete checks — per-crate `--no-run` compiles, workspace build, then per-crate provided-test green — and re-verified foundations before advancing dependents, matching anchor 8 exactly. It reached toward 10 by decomposing the hardest crate (controller-manager) into per-test-binary checkpoints and re-sequencing back into it after workspace tests, but fell short of a full 10 because api-server/scheduler/kubelet were greened as whole crates and no living granular milestone hierarchy was maintained (plan-tool updates were late and sparse).
